Source: http://www.marijuananews.com

Posted January 26, 2000
Special to MarijuanaNews – by Richard Cowan
Vancouver, BC

Today I witnessed Beautiful British Columbia receive the beauty of justice. For someone who sees the ugliness of injustice as much as I do, it was a moving experience. A Provincial court accepted the medical utility of marijuana as a fact, and recognized that it has to come from somewhere.

My very dear friend Hilary Black, the founder of the BC Compassion Club Society, invited me to the sentencing hearing for Marc Richardson, a young friend who is a buyer for the Club.
See
British Columbia Compassion Club Has Almost 900 Members
-- Special To Marijuananews

He had been convicted last June of possession of 6 kilos of marijuana that police found when they searched his vehicle. They also found C$6,000 in cash. The arrest was in North Vancouver, a suburb with its own courts, but policed by the RCMP.

Hilary had testified at the trial that the marijuana and the cash belonged to the club. Indeed, Hilary’s testimony was the principle source of information for the court, and even the prosecution did not question the facts. Actually, the prosecution was only asking for a " large fine " and forfeiture of the cash, not incarceration, even though Marc could have been sentenced to several years in prison. That in itself tells us something important about the status of medical marijuana in the Canadian system. " The Crown " is no longer willing to use harsh sentences to suppress it.

This is not to take a way credit for the defense work. Marc was ably represented by the well-known BC criminal defense lawyer, John Conroy, who has also been representing Renee Boje.

Armed with the information provided by the defense about the Canadian government’s rapidly evolving medical marijuana policies, the Judge had clearly done his home work. In his 14 page decision (which will available on line soon) he cited both the Wakeford and Parker cases, and the fact that the Canadian government is exempting some individuals from the laws prohibiting marijuana possession.
See
One Of The 20 Legal Canadian Medical Marijuana Patients Demands That Government Supply Him With His Medicine – More Pressure on Health Canada
and
Canadian Narks Seize Legal Marijuana User Parker’s Stash;
But They Gave It Back!

Moreover, he was influenced by the Canadian government’s expressed intention to find a supply of medical marijuana. News of this program came after the June trial.
See
Meanwhile In Vancouver, The Supply Problem Seems To Have Been Solved

He summarized the situation by observing that the Canadian government is formally exempting some individuals from the law, and is informally exempting many more. He even cited a statement by the Vancouver police published in the Vancouver Sun on December 14, 1999, that they were aware of the Compassion Club, and that it was " low priority " for them. People are being allowed to use medical marijuana.

The Club is being allowed to sell it, so where is it supposed to come from?

The Judge observed, " Some patients will have to get their medical marijuana from some kind of retail outlet… The pharmacy in this case, known to and tolerated by the police, is the Compassion Club Society. Marijuana will not fall into its hands as manna from heaven. "

In other words, someone has to grow it – illegally, and then it has to be transported – illegally, so saying that people have a right to use it medically is meaningless unless there is a supply. " Marijuana will not fall into its hands as manna from heaven. "

Canadian law says that because of the large amount involved " the minimum sanction which may be imposed is a suspended sentence and probation. " So he suspended sentencing and sentenced Marc to six months of unsupervised probation. For DEAland readers, yes, that means that he will not be required to urinate on command. Crown is not interested in his cannabinoids.

" I consider that it would not reflect a just, peaceful and safe society

to impose a punitive sanction on Mr. Richardson, who acted as nothing more than a conduit for the provision of marijuana for medical purposes. "

He then observed that, inasmuch as the C$6,000 was used by the Club to buy medical marijuana, it was not subject to forfeiture, and should be returned to its " rightful owners! " Unfortunately, the Mounties have already destroyed the Club's marijuana.

The ruling today is not binding on other courts, but its eloquence and substance will certainly influence law enforcement in British Columbia, which has never been more beautiful.

Justice will not fall into our hands as manna from heaven, but we must work for it, as Hilary and her friends have done here in Vancouver.
